answers: lens-performance-code finding 1: not mine — performance cost of two `locked_state_update` calls per iteration is not a requirement in the issue; none of the RQRESU-*/RQLOOP-*/RQFROM-*/RQPATH-*/RQGUAR-*/RQADR-*/RQHYDR-*/RQTEST-*/RQDISP-* requirements govern cycle I/O performance.

lens-red-team-code finding 1: not mine — describes an edge case where `--from-stage <cycle>` with pre-existing `cycle_iterations[cycle].current_iter > 0` could start at the wrong iteration; none of the issue requirements name this scenario, the test fixture writes no `cycle_iterations` key (so the current test does not expose the gap), and fixing it requires code changes beyond my verdict scope.

lens-red-team-code finding 2: not mine — describes a gap in DSRHYD-2 enforcement within the `_cycle_iter_dispatch` member-skip path; it is a correctness concern but not an ISSUE REQUIREMENT; the DSRHYD-2 test at the dispatch-loop level passes, and the gap requires a code change outside the verdict scope.

lens-red-team-code finding 3: not mine — TOCTOU in the `latest`-symlink auto-resume block is a security concern; no ISSUE REQUIREMENT governs the escape-check ordering; it cannot be addressed by my verdict.

lens-correctness-code finding 1: not mine — describes a real edge case where `stage_statuses[$s] == "complete"` survives from iter k-1 and incorrectly skips the first member of iter k when the interruption happened before that member ran in iter k; RQLOOP-1 is met for the tested scenario (interrupted mid-round with at least one member dispatched), and fixing this edge case requires a code change beyond my verdict scope.

lens-correctness-code finding 2: wrong — the finding claims `resume-loop-state-test.sh:272` uses `stage_statuses.test = "in_progress"`, but the diff shows the test at that line writes `'.stage_statuses.build = "complete" | .stage_statuses.test = "aborted"'`; the comment in the same test block explicitly explains why `"aborted"` (not `"in_progress"`) is used: `"in_progress"` is never written by `_cycle_state_write_member_atomic` and would miss the production data shape.

lens-correctness-code finding 3: not mine — single trailing-slash strip with `%%/` in the auto-resume symlink block is a robustness gap; it doesn't affect any issue requirement; fixing it requires a code change outside my verdict scope.

lens-scope-code finding 1: not mine — the `skip_restore=false` branch of `_runner_from_stage_preflight` is in practice dead code: `--from-stage` requires `resume_mode=true` (the guard at line 2313 exits otherwise), and `skip_restore = "$resume_mode"` = `true` at every call site; the S5 test added to address this finding auto-resumes (status=in_progress, fresh timestamp → `get_resume_recommendation` returns `auto_resume`), so it exercises `skip_restore=true`, not `false`; the branch is structurally unreachable, but no ISSUE REQUIREMENT is unmet as a result.
